explanation: Compared against Written on the Wall II (archived all.html and the definitions file wowIIdefs.js from cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/, via the Wayback Machine; the live site does not respond), Conjecture 200 (listed as open, Jan 12, 2006): 'If G is a simple connected graph with n > 1 such that tree(G) = CEIL[1 + λ_avg(G)], then G has a Hamiltonian path', with tree(G) the number of vertices of a largest induced tree and λ_avg the average local independence number. The Lean declaration is the negation of the universal statement (finite nontrivial type, connected G; (largestInducedTreeSize G : ℝ) = ⌈1 + averageIndepNeighbors G⌉ implies a Hamiltonian walk exists). I checked the smallest member of the counterexample family described in the file (graph6 J??FFBRq}N_, 11 vertices) by independent computation: local independence numbers 2,2,2,1,1,1,3,3,3,3,3 (average 24/11, so ⌈1 + λ_avg⌉ = 4), largest induced tree on 4 vertices (exhaustive search over vertex subsets), three pendant vertices and no Hamiltonian path (exhaustive search). So the hypothesis holds and the conclusion fails; the conjecture is false and the negated statement is the correct resolution. Definitions match the source. Faithful. Minor: the question tag is used although the source states a conjecture.
